# File path built from HTTP request data (C#)

`qualor:csharp/path-traversal` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A01:2025 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A01_2025-Broken_Access_Control/), [A01:2021 Broken Access Control](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A01_2021-Broken_Access_Control/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data in ASP.NET Core (MVC and Web API controllers, Minimal APIs, Razor Pages) that
ends up in a file system path:

- `System.IO.File`: the path read, written, appended to, opened, created, deleted, copied, moved
  or replaced (`ReadAllText`, `WriteAllBytesAsync`, `OpenRead`, `Create`, `Delete`, `Copy`,
  `Move`, ...);
- `System.IO.Directory`: the folder created, listed, moved or deleted (`CreateDirectory`,
  `GetFiles`, `EnumerateFiles`, `Delete`, `Move`, ...);
- the `FileStream`, `FileInfo` and `DirectoryInfo` constructors;
- files sent from disk: `PhysicalFile(...)` in controllers and Razor Pages,
  `Results.PhysicalFile`, `TypedResults.PhysicalFile`, `PhysicalFileResult`, and `Results.File`
  with a path.

The value may be used as it is, concatenated, interpolated, or joined with `Path.Combine` or
`Path.Join`. Request data means the parameters of controller actions, Razor Pages handlers and
Minimal API handlers (strings, string arrays, `StringValues`, forms, uploaded files and their
`FileName`, the body stream, and any parameter bound with `[FromQuery]`, `[FromRoute]`,
`[FromForm]`, `[FromHeader]`, `[FromBody]` or `[AsParameters]`), `[BindProperty]` properties, and
the request object itself (`Request.Query`, `Form`, `Headers`, `Cookies`, `RouteValues`, `Path`,
`Body`, ...). Numbers, booleans, GUIDs, dates and enums declared earlier in the file are not
reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
A name such as `../../appsettings.json` climbs out of the intended folder, and a rooted name such
as `/etc/passwd` or `C:\Windows\win.ini` makes `Path.Combine` drop the base folder altogether. The
attacker can then read configuration files and secrets, overwrite application files, or delete
data. The file name of an upload is chosen by the client in the same way.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the requested name is combined with the storage folder and sent back.

```csharp
using System.IO;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class DocumentsController : ControllerBase
{
    private const string Storage = "/var/app/documents";

    [HttpGet("{name}")]
    public IActionResult Get(string name)
    {
        return PhysicalFile(Path.Combine(Storage, name), "application/pdf");
    }
}
```

**Compliant:** the full path is resolved and refused unless it stays inside the storage folder.

```csharp
using System.IO;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class DocumentsController : ControllerBase
{
    private const string Storage = "/var/app/documents/";

    [HttpGet("{name}")]
    public IActionResult Get(string name)
    {
        var full = Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(Storage, name));
        if (!full.StartsWith(Storage, StringComparison.Ordinal))
        {
            return NotFound();
        }
        return PhysicalFile(full, "application/pdf");
    }
}
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- When the request names a file in one folder, keep only its name: `Path.GetFileName(name)`
  removes any folder and root.
- Otherwise resolve the full path with `Path.GetFullPath(Path.Combine(root, name))` and refuse it
  (return or throw) unless it starts with the root folder, written with a trailing separator.
- For uploads, do not use `IFormFile.FileName` as the stored name: generate one with
  `Path.GetRandomFileName()` and keep the client's name only for display.
- Better still, look the file up by an identifier (a number or a key in a fixed table) instead of
  taking a path from the request, or serve files through an `IFileProvider`, which refuses paths
  outside its root.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- ASP.NET Core MVC and Web API
- ASP.NET Core Minimal APIs
- ASP.NET Core Razor Pages
- System.IO

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
Under `qualor dotnet end`, Qualor's Roslyn taint engine runs this rule in OpenGrep's place, on the
projects the build compiled. It follows request data across methods, files and projects, through
properties, expression-bodied members and services registered for dependency injection, and into the
code of compiled Razor views and pages (`.cshtml`), and it reads all C# the compiler accepts. A
finding is of high confidence, or medium ("Possible" in Qualor) when its path goes through data
stored earlier in the request, a lookup by a request key, or a call or view the engine could not
narrow down. The engine's own limits are listed in the [models' README](../../../models/README.md),
section "Known limits". The bullets below are the OpenGrep rule's: it runs outside
`qualor dotnet end`, on C# files no compiled project covers, and as the fallback when the engine
cannot finish.

- Taint is followed through the methods of one file, not into other files. Request data read
  inside an expression-bodied method (`=> ...`) or a property getter is missed.
- Minimal APIs: a class or record parameter bound from the JSON body without `[FromBody]` is not
  taken for request data, and a handler that is a method of another class is missed. A controller
  named `*Controller` whose base class has another name is missed.
- An enum parameter is reported when the enum is declared after its use or in another file. Only
  allow-lists written as `static readonly` tables of literals count; an equality check or
  `Enumerable.Contains(...)` called as a static method does not, and a variable assigned again
  after a check still counts as checked.
- The containment check is recognised in the form shown above: a variable assigned
  `Path.GetFullPath(...)`, then `if (!full.StartsWith(root))` that returns or throws, where `root`
  ends with a directory separator (a string ending in `/` or `\`, or `base +
  Path.DirectorySeparatorChar`); without the separator, `/srv/files` would also admit
  `/srv/files-old`, so such a check is not taken for one. A separator added by string
  interpolation, or a check written as the condition around the use
  (`if (Path.GetFullPath(p).StartsWith(root)) { ... }`), is not recognised either, and the use is
  still reported.
- `StreamReader` and `StreamWriter` given a path are not checked, since their other constructors
  take streams such as the request body.
- `Results.File` given request bytes or a request stream, rather than a path, is reported.
- A value that a method of another class returns for request data (a stored document found by
  its id, a file an image service produced from request options) is taken for request data.
- `ControllerBase.File(virtualPath)` and `IFileProvider.GetFileInfo` are not reported: they
  resolve below the web root and refuse paths outside it. Existence checks (`File.Exists`) are not
  reported either.
- OpenGrep 1.30 does not parse some newer C# syntax (raw strings with `$$"""`, types declared
  without a body such as `class X : Y;`, some multi-line collection expressions); code in those
  parts of a file may be missed.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/csharp/path/path-traversal.cs`](../../../rules/csharp/path/path-traversal.cs) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/csharp/path/path-traversal.yml`](../../../rules/csharp/path/path-traversal.yml), added in version 2026.10.5.
